head.citation-title: Research on grouting connection technology in PHC pipe piles and bearing platform integration
head.abstracts: © 2025 Elsevier LtdThe connection between prestressed high-strength concrete (PHC) pipe piles and bearing platforms is a critical technical issue. To address the issues of the required high precision in traditional bolted connections and the required high craftsmanship in welded connections, this work presents a grouting connection technology that uses large openings in precast bearing platforms. The primary aim of this study was to reduce the difficulty in constructing connections and to ensure connection safety. A series of experimental studies were conducted under compressive loading to discuss the impact of shear keys at the ends of PHC pipe piles and eccentricity on the ultimate bearing capacity of the connection area. The research results indicate that PHC piles with shear keys at the pile ends significantly improve the ultimate bearing capacity of the grouting connection area and reduce the impact of eccentricity on the bearing capacity of the connection area, resulting in plastic failure at the connection area. In PHC piles without shear keys at the pile ends, large eccentricity significantly reduces the ultimate bearing capacity of the grouting connection area, resulting in brittle failure at the connection area. On the basis of experimental and code-based research, a design calculation method for the grouting connection segment is proposed, along with recommended values for the shear key coefficient μ.
